title: Resolve access rules by explicit specificity
prompt: Implement solve(payload) with rules and requests. Each rule has principal, resource, action and effect ("allow" or "deny"); each request has principal, resource and action. Principal/action "*" match any value; other values must match exactly. Resource "*" matches any path; an exact absolute path matches itself; an absolute prefix ending "/*" matches descendants with at least one character after the prefix slash, not the base path itself. Paths are canonical, case-sensitive, contain no "."/".." components or duplicate slashes, and have no trailing slash except root "/". For matching rules, maximize the specificity tuple (resource_kind, resource_prefix_length, principal_is_exact, action_is_exact), lexicographically: exact resource kind=2 with length=len(resource); prefix kind=1 with length=len(resource_without_final_star); "*" kind=0 with length=0. Thus resource specificity takes precedence over principal/action specificity. Among rules tied at maximum specificity, deny wins. No matching rule means deny. Return {"decisions":["allow"|"deny",...]} in request order. Return {"error":"invalid_rule"} before evaluating requests if any rule effect is invalid or its resource pattern is neither "*" nor an absolute path with no wildcard nor an absolute trailing-"/*" pattern with exactly one star. Other fields and path structure are valid. Do not mutate input.
